trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cancun
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Playa Delfines Sunrise Visit
experiences.description: Visit the most iconic public beach in Cancun's Hotel Zone at sunrise for stunning views, soft white sand, and calm morning waves. This is one of the few free public beaches with open ocean views and no resort crowds early in the morning. Bring a towel and enjoy the natural beauty of the Caribbean Sea.

experiences.name: Cancun Street Food Tour in Downtown
experiences.description: Explore the authentic local food scene in downtown Cancun away from the tourist strip. Sample tacos al pastor, fresh ceviche, elotes, marquesitas (crispy crepes), and agua fresca at local markets and street stalls. This is the best way to taste real Mexican cuisine and interact with locals on a budget.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on flight AA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the affordable ADO bus (approx. $10 USD) from the airport to the Hotel Zone. Check in to Cancun Beach Resort and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest public beach access point to get your first taste of the Caribbean. Take a leisurely walk along the shoreline near the hotel, soak in the turquoise waters, and relax on the sand. No cost for public beach access.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to a nearby local taqueria or street food stand close to the hotel zone for an easy, affordable first dinner. Explore the surroundings and get oriented with the area before an early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport before or after landing — airport convenience stores offer affordable options.
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick and cheap meal from a local convenience store (OXXO) or a casual taco stand near the hotel after check-in.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a budget-friendly local taqueria near the Hotel Zone — tacos al pastor or cochinita pibil for around $5–8 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light since you're arriving at 11 AM and will need time for check-in and settling in. Exchange some currency or withdraw pesos from an ATM to have local cash ready for street food and buses throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for the Playa Delfines Sunrise Visit — one of the most iconic and completely free public beaches in Cancun's Hotel Zone. Arrive before sunrise to catch stunning views of the Caribbean, soft white sand, and the famous 'Cancun' sign. This is the best spot for photos with minimal crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: After sunrise, return to the hotel for a quick refresh, then spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing at Playa Delfines or a nearby public beach. Pack sunscreen and water. Explore the beach on foot and enjoy the natural scenery at zero cost.
day_by_day.evening: Take the R1 public bus (about $0.80 USD) downtown for the Cancun Street Food Tour in Downtown Cancun. Explore the authentic local food scene away from the tourist strip — sample tacos, elotes, marquesitas, and other local specialties at very affordable prices.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at a local bakery (panadería) near the hotel — fresh pastries and coffee for under $3 USD.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from a nearby OXXO or local market to enjoy at the beach — fruit cups, chips, and drinks for around $4 USD.
meals.dinner: Street food downtown during the evening tour — budget $8–12 USD for a filling spread of tacos, antojitos, and a fresh agua fresca.

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is a public beach with free access and has a large parking lot and viewing area. The R1 and R2 buses run the full length of the Hotel Zone and into downtown for under $1 USD — the most budget-friendly way to get around.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at Playa Tortugas or Playa Langosta, two free public beaches in the Hotel Zone that are calmer and great for swimming. Arrive early to claim a good spot on the sand. Bring your own water and snacks to avoid overpriced beach vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the bus to Mercado 28 (Market 28) in downtown Cancun — a local market where you can browse handmade crafts, souvenirs, and authentic Mexican goods at much lower prices than Hotel Zone shops. Practice your bargaining skills!
day_by_day.evening: Visit Parque de las Palapas in downtown Cancun, a lively public park that comes alive in the evenings with street performers, local families, food stalls, and live music. Completely free entertainment with a very local vibe.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local comedor (small family restaurant) near the hotel — eggs, beans, tortillas, and coffee for around $4–5 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat lunch at Mercado 28 — the market has several affordable local restaurants inside serving fresh seafood, tacos, and traditional dishes for $6–10 USD.
meals.dinner: Grab street food at Parque de las Palapas — elotes, tacos, tamales, and fresh juices for around $5–7 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Mercado 28 is easily reachable by the downtown R1 bus. Bargaining is expected and welcomed at the market — start at about 50% of the asking price. Parque de las Palapas is most vibrant after 6 PM when locals gather.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to Isla Mujeres via the public ferry from Puerto Juárez (much cheaper than Hotel Zone ferries — about $5–7 USD round trip). Spend the morning exploring the island's stunning Playa Norte, consistently rated one of the best beaches in Mexico, with calm, crystal-clear water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a golf cart (split the cost with fellow travelers — about $40–50 USD for the cart shared among 2–4 people) or rent a bicycle ($10 USD) to explore the island. Visit the southern tip for views and the colorful downtown streets. Browse local shops for affordable souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun on the ferry before sunset. Have a relaxed evening near the hotel — walk along the beach boardwalk and enjoy the night views of the Hotel Zone lagoon.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or grab a torta from a street stand near Puerto Juárez ferry terminal for $2–3 USD.
meals.lunch: Fresh fish tacos or ceviche at a casual beachside restaurant on Isla Mujeres — budget around $8–12 USD for a meal with a drink.
meals.dinner: Simple and affordable dinner at a local taco stand or small restaurant near the hotel — $6–9 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Take the Puerto Juárez ferry (not the Ultramar from the Hotel Zone) to save significantly on ferry costs. Bring cash in pesos for the island as some small vendors don't accept cards. Apply reef-safe sunscreen before swimming in Playa Norte.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed final full morning at your favorite beach — either near the hotel or back at Playa Delfines for one last sunrise or morning swim. Take time to fully enjoy the Caribbean water, collect shells, and soak in the scenery you may have been too busy to appreciate earlier in the week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Laguna Nichupté, the large lagoon behind the Hotel Zone, for a scenic walk or to watch local fishermen. Alternatively, explore the free sections of El Rey Archaeological Zone (small entry fee of about $3 USD) — ancient Mayan ruins located right in the Hotel Zone with iguanas roaming freely.
day_by_day.evening: Head back downtown one final time for dinner and evening drinks. Visit the local craft beer scene or grab a michelada at a neighborhood bar. Browse any last-minute souvenir shopping at Mercado 23, a smaller and more local alternative to Mercado 28.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer breakfast at a local café — chilaquiles or huevos rancheros for $5–7 USD.
meals.lunch: Light lunch of fresh fruit, ceviche tostadas, or a torta from a local stand — $4–6 USD.
meals.dinner: Final dinner at a well-reviewed local restaurant downtown — try cochinita pibil, a Yucatan specialty, for $8–12 USD including a drink.

day_by_day.notes: El Rey Archaeological Zone is a hidden gem that most tourists skip — it's located within the Hotel Zone and is very walkable. Early afternoon is best to avoid peak heat. Mercado 23 is more frequented by locals and has even lower prices than Mercado 28.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final morning swim or walk on the beach near the hotel. Pack your bags and check out. Store luggage at the hotel front desk if your flight is later in the day. Take a last stroll along the Hotel Zone boulevard to soak in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport via the ADO bus (about $10 USD) from the Hotel Zone. Arrive at the airport at least 2–3 hours before your departure flight. Browse duty-free shops for any last-minute gifts — vanilla extract, Kahlua, and Tajín are popular affordable Mexican souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Cancun with incredible beach memories, great food experiences, and a trip completed well within budget. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at a local spot near the hotel — simple and affordable, $4–6 USD. Enjoy fresh tropical fruit if available.
meals.lunch: Grab a meal at a casual restaurant near the hotel before heading to the airport, or pick up snacks for the journey — $5–8 USD.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: The ADO bus stop in the Hotel Zone is near several major hotels and runs regularly to the airport. Confirm your hotel's luggage storage policy the evening before departure. Keep some pesos for the bus and any last-minute purchases — exchange leftover pesos back to USD at the airport if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on flight AA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Cancun Beach Resort in the Hotel Zone. Check-in and settle into your room (request early check-in if available). Take a relaxed first look at the resort facilities and nearby beach stretch.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, head down to the resort beach for a laid-back first afternoon. Swim in the turquoise Caribbean waters, relax on a beach lounger, and get your bearings in the Hotel Zone. Take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront promenade to explore the immediate surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a welcome dinner at a mid-range restaurant close to the Hotel Zone. Try La Habichuela Downtown or a nearby seafood spot for a relaxed introduction to Mexican Caribbean cuisine. End the evening with a walk along the illuminated Hotel Zone boulevard.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at the airport before or after landing — a café sandwich or yogurt parfait to tide you over.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort's beach bar or poolside café — try fish tacos or a fresh ceviche plate (~$12–18 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Parilla or a similar mid-range Mexican restaurant in the Hotel Zone — enchiladas, grilled fish, and fresh agua fresca (~$20–30 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light and flexible since you arrive at 11:00 AM. Don't over-plan — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm your check-in time in advance with Cancun Beach Resort to avoid waiting with luggage. Exchange some currency or withdraw pesos at the airport ATM for small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and head to Playa Delfines for a stunning sunrise visit. This iconic public beach in the Hotel Zone offers breathtaking views of the Caribbean Sea, soft white sand, and the famous 'Cancun' sign — perfect for photos. Arrive around 6:00–6:30 AM to catch the best light. The beach is free and easily accessible by taxi or the Hotel Zone bus (R-1).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a late breakfast, then spend the afternoon exploring Playa Delfines and the surrounding area more leisurely. Alternatively, relax at the resort pool or beach. Visit the nearby Mercado 28 or La Isla Shopping Village for light souvenir browsing and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner at a rooftop or beachfront restaurant in the Hotel Zone. Try Lorenzillo's or a similar mid-range seafood restaurant for fresh lobster, shrimp, or fish dishes with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Early light snack (fruit or granola bar) before sunrise, then a full resort or café breakfast upon return — eggs, fresh fruit, and coffee (~$10–15 USD).
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a local taqueria or food stand near Playa Delfines or back at the resort — fish tacos or a torta (~$8–12 USD).
meals.dinner: Mid-range seafood dinner at Lorenzillo's or similar — grilled fish fillet, rice, salad, and a margarita (~$25–35 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Bring sunscreen, a light jacket for the early morning breeze, and your camera for the sunrise. The Hotel Zone public bus (R-1) is an affordable way to get around (~$0.80 USD per ride). Playa Delfines can get crowded later in the day, so the early morning visit is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day experience: Isla Mujeres Day Trip by Catamaran. Depart from the Hotel Zone marina around 9:00 AM on a catamaran cruise to the beautiful island of Isla Mujeres. Enjoy snorkeling in crystal-clear waters with colorful marine life, swimming, and relaxing on the stunning Playa Norte — consistently ranked among the best beaches in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Isla Mujeres experience. After snorkeling, the catamaran typically stops at the island for free time. Rent a golf cart (~$40–50 USD) to explore the island's charming streets, visit Punta Sur (the southernmost point of Mexico), and browse local artisan shops. Enjoy lunch on the island.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun by catamaran in the late afternoon (usually around 5:00–6:00 PM). Rest at the resort, then head out for a relaxed dinner. Treat yourself to a nice meal to celebrate a great day on the water.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — eggs, toast, juice, and coffee (~$10–15 USD or included with resort stay).
meals.lunch: Lunch on Isla Mujeres at a beachfront restaurant — fresh ceviche, grilled fish, or shrimp tacos with a cold beer (~$15–20 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range Hotel Zone restaurant — try El Fish Fritanga for casual but excellent seafood, or Mocambo for a cozy atmosphere (~$20–28 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Isla Mujeres catamaran trip in advance — popular tours sell out, especially in March (peak season). Most tours are all-inclusive with snorkeling gear, open bar, and snacks (~$60–90 USD per person). Apply reef-safe sunscreen before snorkeling to protect the coral ecosystem. Bring a waterproof bag for your phone and valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Tulum Ruins and Beach Combo. Depart from the hotel around 7:30–8:00 AM for the approximately 2-hour drive south to Tulum. Arrive at the ancient Mayan ruins dramatically perched on a cliff overlooking the turquoise Caribbean Sea. Explore the well-preserved archaeological site with a local guide to learn about Mayan history and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the ruins tour, descend to the stunning beach below the cliffs for a swim and relaxation on one of Mexico's most photogenic beaches. Explore the nearby Tulum beach town or cenotes if time permits. Begin the return drive to Cancun around 4:00–5:00 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Cancun by early evening. Freshen up at the resort, then enjoy a low-key dinner close to the hotel — something casual and satisfying after a full day of sightseeing.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure (~$10–15 USD or included).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Tulum town or at a beachside palapa restaurant — try fresh guacamole, tacos al pastor, or a Yucatecan dish like cochinita pibil (~$12–18 USD).
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at a Hotel Zone restaurant or resort — pizza, burgers, or Mexican comfort food for a relaxed end to a long day (~$15–22 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book a guided tour or rent a car for the Tulum trip. Guided tours (~$60–100 USD per person) include transportation and a guide, which is recommended. If self-driving, the toll road (cuota) is faster and safer. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the ruins and bring a swimsuit for the beach. March is peak season in Tulum — arrive early to beat the crowds. Entrance fee to the ruins is approximately $5–10 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day experience: Xel-Ha All-Inclusive Aquatic Park. Depart from the hotel around 8:00–9:00 AM for the drive south to Xel-Ha, a spectacular natural aquatic theme park built around a stunning coastal lagoon. Snorkel through the lagoon teeming with tropical fish, float down gentle river currents, and explore mangrove trails. The all-inclusive package covers food, drinks, and equipment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Xel-Ha's many attractions — cliff jumping, zip-lining over the lagoon, hammocks in the water, and relaxing on the natural beaches. Take advantage of the all-inclusive food and drink offerings throughout the day.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun by late afternoon. Spend the final evening in style — enjoy a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar in the Hotel Zone, then head out for a special farewell dinner at a nicer restaurant to celebrate the trip.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before departure, or grab something en route (~$8–12 USD).
meals.lunch: Lunch is included in the Xel-Ha all-inclusive package — enjoy fresh seafood, grilled meats, tropical fruits, and unlimited beverages at the park's restaurants.
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner at a mid-range to upscale restaurant — try Harry's Prime Steakhouse, Porfirio's, or La Destilería for a memorable final meal (~$30–45 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Xel-Ha all-inclusive tickets cost approximately $100–130 USD per person — book online in advance for a discount. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only (biodegradable required in the park). Bring water shoes as some surfaces can be rough. The park is about 1.5 hours south of Cancun, near Tulum — consider combining transportation with the previous day's Tulum trip logistics if renting a car.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Cancun. Wake up early for one last sunrise walk on the beach near the resort. Take a final swim in the Caribbean Sea and soak in the last moments of the Hotel Zone atmosphere. Pack up your belongings and check out of Cancun Beach Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Before heading to the airport, join the Cancun Street Food Tour in Downtown for an authentic local experience away from the tourist strip. Explore the real Cancun — sample tacos, elotes, marquesitas (a Yucatecan crepe-like dessert), fresh juices, and other local street food favorites with a knowledgeable guide. This is a great way to experience authentic Mexican culture on your last day.
day_by_day.evening: Depending on your departure flight time, head to Cancun International Airport with enough time for check-in and security. Grab a final coffee or snack at the airport. Depart with wonderful memories of your Cancun adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — enjoy a full spread of eggs, fresh tropical fruit, pastries, and coffee (~$12–18 USD or included with stay).
meals.lunch: Lunch is incorporated into the street food tour experience — you'll graze through multiple food stops covering tacos, antojitos, and local specialties (~$35–50 USD per person for the tour).
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a light meal before your flight — opt for a sit-down airport restaurant for a final taste of Mexican food (~$15–20 USD).

day_by_day.notes: The Cancun Street Food Tour typically runs 3–4 hours — book a morning or early afternoon slot to ensure you have plenty of time before your flight. Confirm your flight departure time and factor in at least 2.5–3 hours for airport arrival before international flights. Keep some pesos handy for last-minute tips, small purchases, or airport incidentals. Don't forget to declare any food items you may be bringing home.

day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, head down to the resort's private beach for your first taste of the Caribbean. Relax on a premium lounger with butler service, take a dip in the turquoise waters, and soak in the Hotel Zone atmosphere. Optional: book a 60-minute welcome massage at the resort spa to recover from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset cocktail at the resort's oceanfront bar, then head to dinner at La Habichuela Sunset — one of Cancun's most celebrated fine-dining restaurants known for its Caribbean-Mexican fusion cuisine and elegant garden setting.

meals.breakfast: Light snack or coffee at the airport or upon arrival at the resort's welcome lounge
meals.lunch: Casual beachside dining at the resort's signature beach club restaurant — fresh ceviche, guacamole, and grilled fish tacos with craft cocktails
meals.dinner: La Habichuela Sunset — try the Cocobichuela (lobster and shrimp in a tamarind-chipotle sauce served in a coconut) paired with a premium margarita or local mezcal

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep the schedule light and relaxed. Confirm spa and restaurant reservations for the rest of the week. Ensure all excursion bookings are confirmed with the concierge. Sun protection and reef-safe sunscreen are essential from day one.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for the Playa Delfines Sunrise Visit. Arrive at Cancun's most iconic public beach before 6:30 AM to witness a breathtaking Caribbean sunrise over the soft white sands. The beach offers panoramic views of the turquoise sea and the famous Cancun sign — perfect for photography. Bring a light jacket as early mornings can be breezy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a late breakfast, then spend the afternoon at the resort's luxury pool and beach facilities. Arrange a private cabana with personalized butler service. Try paddleboarding or a resort-offered snorkeling session along the Hotel Zone reef. Optional: visit the resort's boutique spa for a hydrotherapy circuit.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Harry's Prime Steakhouse & Raw Bar in the Hotel Zone — one of Cancun's premier luxury dining destinations with premium cuts, fresh seafood towers, and an extensive wine cellar. Pair your meal with a bottle from their curated cellar.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet resort breakfast buffet or à la carte eggs Benedict with smoked salmon at the resort's main restaurant
meals.lunch: Light poolside bites — shrimp skewers, fresh fruit platters, and premium cocktails at the resort's pool bar
meals.dinner: Harry's Prime Steakhouse & Raw Bar — USDA Prime ribeye or a chilled seafood tower, accompanied by a fine Malbec or Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon

day_by_day.notes: Set an early alarm for the sunrise visit — aim to arrive at Playa Delfines no later than 6:15 AM. Arrange private transportation through the concierge. The beach is free and public but arrives quickly at dawn. Bring a camera and comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Isla Mujeres Day Trip by Catamaran. Depart from the Hotel Zone marina by 9:00 AM aboard a premium catamaran. Enjoy open bar and light snacks on the sail over. Upon arrival, snorkel in the crystal-clear waters of MUSA (Underwater Museum of Art) or the natural reef, exploring vibrant coral and tropical fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Isla Mujeres and explore the charming island at leisure. Rent a golf cart to tour the island, visit Punta Sur (the southernmost point with dramatic cliffs and a sculpture garden), and relax on Playa Norte — consistently rated one of the best beaches in the Caribbean with calm, shallow turquoise water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun by catamaran as the sun begins to set — enjoy a festive atmosphere on board with music and cocktails. Back at the resort, freshen up and dine at Lorenzillo's, a legendary Cancun restaurant built over the lagoon, specializing in fresh Caribbean lobster.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — continental spread with fresh tropical fruits, pastries, and espresso
meals.lunch: Beachfront lunch on Isla Mujeres at Mango Café or Sunset Grill — fresh grilled fish, lobster tacos, and coconut shrimp with a cold local beer or frozen piña colada
meals.dinner: Lorenzillo's — whole Caribbean lobster grilled to perfection, served with garlic butter and sides, paired with a crisp Chardonnay or premium rosé

day_by_day.notes: Confirm catamaran departure time with the concierge the evening before. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a light cover-up, waterproof sandals, and a dry bag for valuables. Premium catamaran tours typically include open bar, snorkel gear, and a guide. Book Lorenzillo's in advance as it is a popular reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Tulum Ruins and Beach Combo. Depart by private luxury vehicle at 8:00 AM for the approximately 1.5-hour drive south. Arrive at the Tulum archaeological site early to beat the crowds. Explore the remarkably preserved Mayan ruins dramatically perched on a cliff overlooking the Caribbean Sea — one of the most photogenic archaeological sites in all of Mexico.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the ruins tour, descend to Tulum Beach — a stunning stretch of white sand below the cliffs. Spend the afternoon at one of Tulum's upscale beach clubs such as Ahau Tulum or Nomade, enjoying luxury loungers, fresh cocktails, and the wild, natural beauty of the Tulum coastline. Optional: explore the bohemian Tulum Pueblo or beach strip boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun by private transfer (approximately 1.5 hours). Freshen up at the resort, then enjoy a refined dinner at Porfirio's Cancun — a sophisticated Mexican restaurant with stunning lagoon views, exceptional guacamole prepared tableside, and premium tequila and mezcal selections.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure — fresh juice, yogurt parfait, and avocado toast
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Tulum beach club — fresh ceviche, grilled octopus, and tropical cocktails with your feet in the sand
meals.dinner: Porfirio's Cancun — tableside guacamole, duck carnitas tacos, and a premium mezcal flight or signature margarita

day_by_day.notes: Book a private guided tour of Tulum ruins for the best experience — guides bring the history to life. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the ruins, then switch to sandals for the beach. Bring cash in Mexican pesos for tips and small purchases in Tulum Pueblo. Depart early to maximize time at both the ruins and beach.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Xel-Ha All-Inclusive Aquatic Park experience. Depart by private transfer at 8:30 AM for the natural aquatic park located between Cancun and Tulum. Xel-Ha is built around a stunning coastal lagoon where freshwater cenotes meet the Caribbean Sea. Begin the morning with snorkeling through the lagoon's natural channels, spotting tropical fish, rays, and sea turtles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Xel-Ha's many attractions: cliff jumping platforms, zip-lines over the water, floating in the lazy river, and exploring hidden coves and cenote swimming holes. The all-inclusive package covers unlimited food and beverages — enjoy fresh seafood, tropical drinks, and local specialties throughout the day. Rent snorkel gear upgrades or a private float for enhanced comfort.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort in the late afternoon, refreshed and sun-kissed. Treat yourself to a premium couples' or individual spa treatment at the resort spa — a deep tissue massage, aloe wrap, or signature Caribbean ritual. End the evening with a romantic dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant, enjoying the ocean breeze and starlit sky.

meals.breakfast: Light resort breakfast before departure — fresh fruit smoothie, granola, and coffee
meals.lunch: All-inclusive dining at Xel-Ha — grilled fish, fresh guacamole, ceviche, and unlimited tropical beverages included in the park package
meals.dinner: Resort signature fine-dining restaurant — chef's tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring seasonal Mexican and Caribbean-inspired dishes

day_by_day.notes: Book Xel-Ha tickets in advance through the concierge for the best rates and private transport. The park opens at 8:30 AM — arriving early ensures access to the best snorkeling spots before crowds build. Bring reef-safe sunscreen (required by the park), a waterproof camera, and water shoes. The all-inclusive package covers food, drinks, snorkel gear, and most activities.

day_by_day.morning: On your final morning, take the Cancun Street Food Tour in Downtown for an authentic cultural experience away from the Hotel Zone. Depart at 9:00 AM with a private guide to explore the vibrant local markets and street stalls of downtown Cancun. Sample handmade tacos al pastor, marquesitas (crispy rolled crepes), fresh tropical juices, and regional Yucatecan specialties like cochinita pibil.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a final leisurely afternoon on the beach or by the pool. Enjoy one last swim in the Caribbean, take photos, and soak in the beauty of the Hotel Zone. Visit the resort's boutique for any last-minute gifts or souvenirs. Optional: arrange a final spa treatment or private yoga session on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Tempo by Heinz Beck — one of Cancun's most prestigious fine-dining establishments, offering contemporary Mediterranean cuisine with Caribbean influences. This Michelin-recognized chef's restaurant delivers an unforgettable final evening. Enjoy a multi-course tasting menu with premium wine pairings as a perfect conclusion to a luxury Cancun escape.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet à la carte breakfast at the resort — eggs Florentine, fresh-squeezed juices, and artisan pastries
meals.lunch: Street food tastings throughout the downtown tour — tacos, marquesitas, fresh agua frescas, and local snacks are the meal
meals.dinner: Tempo by Heinz Beck — multi-course tasting menu with wine pairing; reserve the chef's table experience for an intimate, elevated farewell dinner

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure logistics with the concierge on this final day — arrange private luxury airport transfer for your departure. Pack the evening before to maximize your final day. The street food tour is a wonderful cultural contrast to the luxury resort experience and provides an authentic memory of Mexico. Tip guides and service staff generously as a final gesture of appreciation.
